assessments.evidence: lockIntent serializes through the existing per-job/key write lock and re-reads the intent. One MATERIALIZED outcome_clock supplies both eligibility and observed_at. The conditional UPDATE requires running state, exact current claim ID/BIGINT fence, possible_dispatch=1 and live lease/execution/lifetime at the SQL sample. Neither pending nor stale/expired claims can manufacture success or explicit unknown. Receipt storage takes payload_version from the updated immutable intent, not a caller-supplied version.

The state decision is made in SQL, not against an old host snapshot. Expiry before state SQL rejects the update and later checked claim recovery becomes unknown. If SQL qualifies while live, return latency alone does not discard a known acknowledgement: the receipt and succeeded state remain eligible for the same transaction commit. This differs correctly from granting a new work/renewal handle after expiry. It does not promise survival of an outer rollback, inherited operational deadline, transport fault, process crash or uncertain COMMIT.

assessments.area: State/receipt atomicity when outer host catches a fault
assessments.evidence: acknowledge runs schema/conditional state/receipt insert through the generated client's nested transaction method. Root entry first rejects a non-live capability; its lazy callback invokes the initialized client only when called. A real receipt PRIMARY KEY fault after succeeded UPDATE caused ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT and RELEASE, restoring running while the outer host continued and committed an unrelated mutation. Outer rollback also removes caller authority changes, state and receipt together. SQLite nested transaction branch was extracted verbatim from current target.rs and executed in the independent probe; PostgreSQL savepoint branch was inspected and its actual generated-host suite result is attributed separately.

assessments.area: Closed reference receipt and time trust
assessments.evidence: Only a plain Object-prototype object with exactly one own key and an accepted_at data descriptor is accepted. Exact millisecond UTC syntax and Date round-trip reject malformed/calendar-normalized values without invoking an accessor. accepted_at is copied as provider evidence; observed_at is the SQL database-time sample and neither receipt age nor provider clock controls identity, fences or key ordering. A shape-valid host-created receipt is not trustworthy provider evidence.

assessments.area: Known success release versus conservative unknown
assessments.evidence: The paired receipt and succeeded transition release only the original intent's FIFO block after outer COMMIT; repeated acknowledgement cannot rewrite the stored receipt. record_delivery_unknown changes only the current possible-effect intent and leaves later same-key intent blocked. Unknown cannot be acknowledged or replayed via this primitive; trusted late reconciliation remains a separate privileged future surface. Renewal/count/fence/possible-marker budgets are not reset by either transition.

retainedLimits: This is a private host-state foundation, not evidence that a provider issued a receipt. Future compiler binding must accept only checked SERVICE-001 exact-key/immutable-payload adapter outcomes and current authorized job context. Shape-valid arbitrary host values cannot establish provider acceptance, policy authority or trusted reconciliation.

Only reference mail accepted_at is reviewed. No generic receipt typing, supported-handler/version decoding, provider invocation, public grammar/operator authority, worker scheduler/heartbeat, crash-to-provider conformance, safe retry/dead-letter/attempt history or complete 18-case ASYNC approval. Whole RM-306 remains incomplete.

Success applies to the immutable original intent. The future golden completion binding must separately guard source revision, recipient/effect policy and reminder_sent_at. A host catching an acknowledgement fault can still commit unrelated outer mutations; the inner savepoint pairs state/receipt, not arbitrary caller mutations outside it. No newer revision sent-mark or policy-bypass authority approved.

The eligible SQL sample is not outer COMMIT acknowledgement. Source rollback, inherited operational deadline/cancellation, storage/transport error or crash can still prevent durable completion; uncertain commit/outcome must never justify blind resend. Known lease-eligible decision survives ordinary return latency in the tested unexpired transaction context, not every surrounding failure. Trusted late receipt resolution after unknown remains future work.

Live capability, fencing and database-time assumptions from previous reviews remain. The token does not interrupt already-running I/O, drain detached work or replace awaiting all transaction operations. Supported clock sampling is not physical clock-regression, final-response freshness or hard-preemption assurance.

Lazy CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is not schema attestation/migration. Compatible compiler-owned claim and receipt layouts, backend/key/foreign-key constraints, restored-record validity, UUID collisions, numeric/calendar ranges and default/golden limits remain separate gates. No public receipt read/repair or malformed restored-schema approval.
